title: Jerusalem
summary: The city of David, temple center, and prophetic symbol of God’s reign, judgment, and future restoration.
historical_context: Jerusalem moves from Jebusite city to Davidic capital and temple center, then becomes the focal point of exile, return, and messianic expectation.
ancient_near_east_context: As a royal and cultic center in the southern Levant, Jerusalem sits at the intersection of kingship, worship, and imperial pressure.
literary_context: The city functions as geography, theology, and eschatological symbol across the Old and New Testaments.
covenantal_significance: Jerusalem concentrates Davidic kingship, temple worship, covenant judgment, and prophetic hope in one place.
interpretive_notes: Jerusalem is both a literal city and a theological symbol; keep those uses distinct but connected.
Prophetic and apocalyptic references to Jerusalem often layer present history with future hope.
common_questions: Why is Jerusalem so important in the Bible?
How does Jerusalem connect David, the temple, and the New Testament?
Why is Jerusalem also a symbol of hope?
